> 知北遊於玄水之上，登隱弅之丘，而適遭無為謂焉。

Knowledge travels north, crosses the dark water, climbs the hidden mound, and happens to meet No-Action-No-Word.

Then he asks three questions: what to think, where to dwell, by what path to get the way. Three questions, and the answer is silence — not refusal, but 不知答也: no answer available to give.

## The name is the argument

This is the only chapter in the book where nearly every character is abstraction: 無為謂, 狂屈, 泰清, 無窮, 無為, 無始, 光曜, 無有.

Read the names as the argument, and the geography becomes readable too. 玄水 is dark water; 白水 is bright water; 狐閕 is the doubtful; 帝宮 is the highest human knowledge.

知 walks from dark to bright, from doubt to certainty — and gets further away the whole way. That is the chapter's plot, and it is a plot about method.

## 無思無慮, 無處無服, 無從無道

Three 無s answering three questions.

The questions ask for a method. The answer removes the method's category: there is no 思 to perform, no place to stay, no path to take.

Note that 黃帝 gives the answer as 無, not as "how." Most spiritual instruction reverses this — it answers "how" and leaves the category intact. This chapter does not.

## 道不可致，德不可至

致: to summon, to send for. 至: to arrive at.

The way cannot be sent for. Virtue cannot be arrived at. Both verbs are verbs of acquisition, and both fail.

## 仁可為也，義可虧也，禮相偽也

Three levels, degrading: benevolence can still be done; rightness already loses something when done; ritual is mutual pretending.

Then 禮者，道之華而亂之首也 — ritual is the flower of the way and the head of disorder. 華: the flowering surface, the part that shows. 亂之首: the beginning of confusion, not its worst point.

This is 老子 chapter 38 rewritten in one paragraph, and the ordering (道, 德, 仁, 義, 禮) is the same.

## 為道者日損

The direction of the work is subtraction. 損: to decrease.

Every other curriculum in the world is a 益. This one opens with the instruction to lose something each day, and the thing to lose is not pleasure. It is 為 — the doing, the making, the produced layer.

## 通天下一氣耳

One breath through the whole world.

This is almost always quoted as "everything is one," and the sentence just before it forbids that reading: 臭腐復化為神奇，神奇復化為臭腐 — the rotten turns into the wondrous, the wondrous turns back into the rotten.

So 一氣 is not "all things are the same." It is: all things are the same batch of material changing form. The unity is in the substrate, not in the appearance.

Which is why the next line says 聖人故貴一 — the sage values the one, not sameness.

## 大美、明法、成理

Beauty that is 大, law that is 明, order that is 成 — already complete, already running.

The three words share a property: none of them needs a person to say them. That is the test this chapter applies to every claim about the world.

## The test

Take one practice you do to become clearer. Then ask the 損 question: what has it removed this month? If the answer is nothing — only additions — the direction is wrong, and more effort will deepen it.
